from_quote: I beg leave to offer one or two short remarks on a production which appeared in your last, under the signature of Agrippa.
rationale: Answers "a production which appeared in your last, under the signature of Agrippa"; the previous Gazette (Tuesday, November 27, 1787) carried Agrippa 2, and the words Cassius goes on to quote are in it.

from_quote: I wish to say nothing of the merits or demerits of individuals, such arguments always do hurt.
rationale: Quotes Agrippa's words "I wish to say nothing of the merits or demerits of individuals, such arguments always do hurt," and his "the attempt has been made to deprive us," both from this paragraph ("wi.sh" is OCR damage in the target).
to_quote: to say nothing of the merits or demerits of individuals; such arguments always do hurt.

from_quote: from their cradles, been incapable of comprehending any other principles of government than those of absolute power, and who have, in this instance (meaning the form of government proposed by them) attempted to deprive the people of their constitutional liberty by a pitiful trick.
rationale: Quotes, with small changes and an inserted gloss, Agrippa's words about persons who "from their cradles" have been "incapable of comprehending any other principles of government" and tried to deprive the people "of their constitutional liberty, by a pitiful trick."
to_quote: from their cradles been incapable of comprehending any other principles of government, than those of absolute power, and who have, in this very affair, tried to deprive them of their constitutional liberty, by a pitiful trick.

from_quote: he insinuates, that the members of the late federal convention are incapable of comprehending any other principles of government than those of absolute power
rationale: States Agrippa's claim that the convention's members are "incapable of comprehending any other principles of government than those of absolute power" and sets out to answer it by the examples of Washington and Franklin; the claim is in this paragraph of Agrippa 2, identified from the date and the words quoted in Cassius.6.3.
